subject.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this fenced runtime-retirement and harness-reset path as the canonical recovery after reply-session conflict retries are exhausted?
rationale: The implementation is correct and well-proven, but its last-resort recovery deliberately aborts competing work and resets shared runtime state, so accepting that lifecycle contract requires human ownership judgment.

options.title: Land Fenced Recovery
options.body: Accept the bounded interruption tradeoff because the branch revalidates before draining, reuses established lifecycle primitives, and demonstrates successful live recovery.

options.title: Require Broader Live Proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until another busy channel demonstrates that recovery restores the wedged session without suppressing unrelated delivery.

recommendation.title: Land Fenced Recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded interruption tradeoff because the branch revalidates before draining, reuses established lifecycle primitives, and demonstrates successful live recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior merged work is closest to the guarded reply-session initialization and transcript-continuity boundary affected by this choice.
